Hi Connor — thanks for the clear recap.

Short answers:
1) We treat any user-provided identifying information as PII—names, emails, order IDs count. Free-text chat that might incidentally include PII should also be treated conservatively.
2) We require max 30-day retention for request/response content. Longer-term logs (aggregates/metrics) are fine for 12 months.
3) EU-only residency is required for European customers; for US customers US residency is fine. For the demo we want to see EU hosting options.
4) We do not require token-level logs; aggregated telemetry and request-level hashes for debugging are acceptable as long as the raw prompt/output can be disabled for retention.

I'll attach our minimal security requirements doc that the procurement team will use in the review.

Ellie

Connor / Rishi / Ellie — quick technical answers below. Happy to run the 30-min deep-dive to walk through specifics.

Summary (short answers):
- Hosted API (standard): By default we retain request and response payloads for 30 days for abuse detection and quality monitoring. These logs are encrypted at rest and accessible only to engineering on a need basis.
- Opt-out / retention controls: Paid customers (Dedicated or higher-tier Hosted) can request prompt/output retention opt-out; we also offer a 'no retention' contract addendum for customers that need it. In Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) there is no vendor-stored prompt/output by default—data stays in the customer environment.
- Token-level logging: Disabled by default for customer-visible telemetry. Token-level traces can be enabled in a controlled way for debugging under a support ticket and with explicit customer approval; these are time-limited and audited.
- KV cache and streaming state: Ephemeral in-memory cache used during live sessions only; not persisted to disk and not stored in customer logs unless explicitly requested.
- Audit logs & evidence: We can produce request/response retention reports and access logs for the requested window; SOC 2 summary and DPA draft available. See attachments.
- Data residency: Hosted regions include US and EU (Frankfurt). Customers may pin production traffic to an EU region. Dedicated pools can be provisioned in customer-preferred regions. Private deployments run in customer network.

Attachments I’m including:
- security-snapshot-PII-table.xlsx (breakdown: what we store by feature + retention defaults)
- redwood-data-flow-diagram.pdf (same flow with residency notes)
